newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Faulding will still make Neutrogena.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Faulding will still make Neutrogena.

text.p: Pharmaceutical company F.H Faulding and Co Ltd said on Thursday it would continue to manufacture the Neutrogena skin care and beauty products range following the sale of its Australian and New Zealand trademarks to Johnson and Johnson Pacific.

Company secretary Rod McNeil told Reuters that Faulding's Neutrogena trademark was constrained to Australia and New Zealand which did not fit the company's strategic focus on products which could be marketed throughout the world.
The sale also reflected a move by the company's consumer products division to self-medication products away from health and beauty lines, he said.

McNeil said he could not reveal the value of the sale of the trademark to Johnson and Johnson Pacific but said the brand had been a significant part of Faulding's consumer products division since the 1960s.
"It is not more than ten percent of our total business in that division, so it is a quite significant brand but, on the other hand, it is not dominant," he said.
McNeil said Johnson and Johnson would also utilise Faulding's facilities to contract manufacture additional products in their range.
Johnson and Johnson (United States) purchased the worldwide operations of Neutrogena in late 1994.
